name: Amiza
classification_notes: Single-weight decorative display face built from flowing, wave-like curves referencing psychedelic lettering, art nouveau ornament and Y2K aesthetics. No weight variation, condensed, italic or mono variants. Basic Extended Latin with PUA-encoded characters and ligatures; 83–85 glyphs total.
summary: A single-weight decorative display face from Indonesian studio Zarma Type, built on wavy, bubbly letterforms drawn from psychedelic lettering and art nouveau traditions, suited to bold branding and editorial headlines.
description: Amiza is constructed from flowing, wave-like curves that draw on psychedelic lettering traditions and art nouveau ornament, giving the face a distinctive groovy personality. It ships as a single weight with Extended Latin support and roughly 85 glyphs, best deployed at large sizes where its intricate decorative detail can read clearly. Its natural territory is logo design, branding and editorial headlines where a retro or Y2K character is the brief.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Amiza as a versatile font inspired by psychedelic and experimental typefaces, combining mesmerising curves with intricate details to balance elegance and boldness. The foundry positions it for branding, editorial design and eye-catching headlines, noting that it commands attention at display sizes. Commercial licences are available at multiple tiers through the studio's own site.

name: Anerome
classification_notes: Three-variant decorative family built on aged serif letterforms. No conventional weight axis – the three styles (Regular, Rough, Stamped) apply progressive distress treatments to the same underlying drawing. Feels closer to a lettering revival than a systematic type family.
summary: A vintage display family in three distress variants – clean, rough and stamped – suited to badge logos, posters and print branding with a period-press character.
description: Anerome offers three takes on the same aged serif letterforms: Regular keeps the forms clean, Rough adds organic edge degradation, and Stamped simulates an uneven press impression. The family ships with over 300 glyphs, covering stylistic alternates and discretionary ligatures accessed through OpenType-capable applications. It is best used at display scale for logotypes, packaging and poster headlines where a handcrafted or letterpress quality is the intent.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type presents Anerome as a vintage display typeface with an authentic period aesthetic, built around three complementary style fonts and a glyph set exceeding 300 characters. The foundry highlights its stylistic alternates and discretionary ligatures, and recommends it for branding materials, logos, posters, business cards and apparel graphics – noting that OpenType-aware software is required to access the full character set.

name: Arinoe
classification_notes: All-caps display typeface with sans-serif bones dressed in a rustic, handcrafted aesthetic. The four-style family covers a clean Regular plus three textured treatments (Outline, Rough, Stamped), making it structurally a display sans but marketed and used as a vintage/grunge display face. No true italic or condensed – the stylistic variants are texture-based, not axis-based.
summary: A four-style vintage display face from Indonesian foundry Zarma Type, built around rustic all-caps letterforms with textured variants and extensive OpenType alternates for branding, posters and apparel graphics.
description: Arinoe is a vintage display typeface designed for projects that call for a handcrafted, rustic character. The family ships in four stylistic variants – Regular, Outline, Rough and Stamped – giving designers ready-made texture without post-processing. It includes an extended Latin character set with OpenType alternates, ligatures and PUA-encoded glyphs, suited to heritage-style branding, apparel graphics and signage.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type is an independent Indonesian foundry producing distinctive display typefaces. Arinoe brings uniqueness and authenticity to every character through its rustic vintage charm, with a wealth of alternate characters and ligatures offering designers extensive room to experiment on creative projects.

name: Ayuga
classification_notes: Bold, thick display letterforms with a groovy retro-psychedelic character. Single weight only. No italic, condensed or mono variants. Designed for high-contrast, attention-grabbing use rather than text setting.
summary: A single-weight display typeface with bold, thick letterforms and a groovy retro-psychedelic character, suited to logos, posters and hipster-adjacent branding.
description: Ayuga is a display typeface from Zarma Type's Azzam Ridhamalik, built around bold, thick letterforms with a distinctly groovy, vintage flavour. It covers Latin Extended-A with 381 glyphs, including ligatures and PUA-encoded characters, and suits high-contrast applications: logos, posters and branding work with a psychedelic or retro edge. There are no italic, condensed or mono variants.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type positions Ayuga as a display typeface blending retro and psychedelic aesthetics, with bold letterforms built to make designs stand out from the crowd. The foundry targets it at modern branding, logo design, hipster-themed visuals and poster work.

name: Bilgres
classification_notes: Single-style bold display face with exaggerated rounded edges, wide proportions and miniature counters. Classified as sans-serif display with a groovy, retro character drawn from 1960s–70s pop art and hippie aesthetics. Includes OpenType features and PUA-encoded characters.
summary: A single-weight rounded display face with a bold, wide footprint and a distinctly sixties groovy personality, suited to retro-leaning posters, album covers and branding.
description: Bilgres is a bold, wide display typeface built around exaggerated rounded edges and miniature counters that give it an immediately retro, pop-art quality. Released in 2024 by Indonesian foundry Zarma Type, it covers a single weight and is designed for high-impact use – posters, album covers, logos and social media graphics. The hippie-inspired character sits comfortably alongside sixties and seventies visual references.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describe Bilgres as a hippie-themed typeface that pairs strong and gentle shapes through rounded edges to produce a bold, wide font with a playful, funky personality. It was made for eye-catching work: posters, album covers, logos, social media graphics, branding and packaging.

name: Borneo Amber
classification_notes: All-caps display face with bold geometric letterforms softened by subtle vintage curves. Ships in two texture variants: a smooth Clean style and a distressed Rough style that introduces handcrafted, organic character. No lowercase, no italics, no condensed cut.
summary: An all-caps display face pairing bold geometry with soft vintage curves, offered in Clean and Rough variants for retro-leaning brand and packaging work.
description: Borneo Amber was released in October 2025 by Azzam Ridhamalik of Zarma Type, a small foundry based in Sukoharjo, Central Java. The face is all-caps only, built on confident geometric structure with curves that read as both industrial and approachable. The Rough variant adds distressed texture for labels, posters and retro signage, while the Clean style suits more polished brand applications.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type positions Borneo Amber as a modern vintage font combining the warmth of nostalgia with bold contemporary design. The structured letterforms merge clean geometry with soft curves, and the two-variant approach – Clean for polished sophistication, Rough for organic charm – is intended to give designers flexibility across brand identity, product packaging and retro editorial contexts.

name: Bright Supply
classification_notes: Thick, rounded bold brush script with two style variants – Regular (polished, clean strokes) and Organic (surface texture for a handmade feel). PUA encoded; includes ligatures, swash characters and stylistic alternates. Designed for display-scale use.
summary: A bold brush script in two variants – clean and textured – built for display use in branding, packaging and café-style graphics.
description: Bright Supply is a thick, flowing bold script with rounded strokes and strong handcrafted energy. It ships in two styles: Regular, which reads clean and polished for professional branding, and Organic, which adds surface texture suited to artisanal packaging and café menus. The character set includes ligatures, swashes and stylistic alternates, with PUA encoding for easy access outside OpenType-aware applications.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Bright Supply as a warm, confident bold script built for branding that needs a handmade quality. The Regular style suits polished professional work; the Organic variant offers a softer, more expressive texture for bakeries, cafés and beverage labels.

name: Bringbold Nineties
classification_notes: Bold display serif with chunky letterforms, sharp serifs and tight spacing, designed to evoke 90s headline and marquee typography. Two styles only: Regular and an oblique Slanted variant. No true italic. PUA-encoded alternates, swashes and ligatures via OpenType.
summary: A chunky 90s-inflected bold display serif with sharp serifs and tight spacing, built for retro branding, editorial headers and vintage poster work.
description: Bringbold Nineties draws on 90s headline typography – flashy marquee letters and vintage editorial layouts – rendered as a contemporary display serif. Chunky letterforms, tight spacing and sharp serifs produce a strong visual rhythm suited to headers, album covers and retro branding. It ships in Regular and Slanted styles with broad OpenType support including stylistic alternates, decorative swashes and ligatures.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type positions Bringbold Nineties as a classic serif that captures the essence of 90s retro design with a modern twist, combining strong bold characteristics and crisp serif details to strike a balance between vintage nostalgia and contemporary readability.

name: Buccario
classification_notes: Display serif with reversed contrast details and a high-legibility structure despite its decorative intent. Ships in four stylistic variants (Regular, Inked, Outline, Inked Outline) rather than traditional weight grades. Targets retro and vintage aesthetics; not suited to body text.
summary: A vintage-inflected display serif with reversed contrast and four stylistic variants, built for retro branding, packaging and editorial headers.
description: Buccario is a display serif by Azzam Ridhamalik, drawn with reversed contrast details and a high-legibility structure despite its decorative character. It ships in four stylistic variants – Regular, Inked, Outline and Inked Outline – giving designers flexibility for logo work, packaging and editorial headers. Its OpenType feature set includes alternates, discretionary ligatures and PUA characters, with support for over 100 languages.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describe Buccario as an elegant serif that brings a fresh twist to retro and vintage design, blending classic elegance with modern appeal through sophisticated curves, reversed contrast and high-legibility structure. Versatility comes through alternates, ligatures and decorative touches, making it suited to branding projects, bold headlines, nostalgic packaging and stylish editorial spreads.

name: Bulbis
classification_notes: Bubble display typeface with graffiti and street art roots. Three structural variants rather than weight range: Outline, Filled and Anti-Counter, each rendering the same buoyant letterform with different opacity and depth. No italics, no condensed, no mono companion. Extended Latin glyph set with PUA encoded characters and OpenType support.
summary: A graffiti-rooted bubble display typeface from Zarma Type, available in three structural variants: Outline, Filled and Anti-Counter.
description: Bulbis is a bold bubble display typeface designed by Azzam Ridhamalik for Zarma Type in 2023, rooted in graffiti and street art with an explicit y2k and streetwear sensibility. It comes in three structural variants — Outline, Filled and Anti-Counter — each applying a different treatment to the same rounded, buoyant letterform. The extended Latin character set covers European languages, though its appeal is entirely decorative: logos, brand marks and social media graphics where that aesthetic is the brief.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describe Bulbis as a bubble graffiti font blending y2k culture with streetwear visuals, suited to logos, branding and social media work where a bold, modern display look is needed.

name: Chunko Bold
classification_notes: Single-weight geometric display sans with chunky proportions, low stroke contrast and pronounced rounded terminals throughout. High x-height and generous weight give it strong presence at display sizes. PUA-encoded characters, stylistic alternates, and standard and discretionary ligatures included via OpenType.
summary: A chunky geometric display sans with rounded terminals and a single bold weight, suited to branding, packaging and poster work that relies on type to carry visual weight.
description: Chunko Bold is a display typeface from Zarma Type, an independent Indonesian foundry, released in 2025. It has chunky proportions, low stroke contrast and rounded terminals throughout, making it well suited to headlines, packaging and large-scale typographic compositions. The character set covers extended Latin with diacritical marks; OpenType features include stylistic alternates and standard and discretionary ligatures.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type is an independent display type foundry based in Sukoharjo, Central Java, founded by Azzam Ridhamalik. It specialises in display typefaces across serif, sans-serif and script categories, producing fonts aimed at branding, packaging and editorial work for designers who want their projects to stand out.

name: Entuista
classification_notes: Squared, chunky geometric letterforms with a 60s–70s retro sensibility. Strictly a display face — not suited to body text. Includes oblique (mechanically slanted) variants and pre-built extrude styles. The extrude versions ship as separate font files rather than OpenType features.
summary: A squat, chunky display typeface with a groovy retro character, suited to bold branding in sport, music and vintage-adjacent contexts.
description: Entuista is a chunky geometric display typeface built around squared letterforms with a 60s–70s retro sensibility. It ships in four styles — Regular, Oblique and pre-extruded versions of each — removing the need to apply manual 3D effects in design software. Best deployed at large sizes for headlines, logos and branding where a bold, vintage-inflected personality is the brief.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Entuista as a squary and chunky typeface with a touch of unique retro style, built for display use. The pre-built extrude versions are included to save production time, doing away with manual extrusion effects in design applications.

name: Galvitra
classification_notes: Grotesk-based display typeface with selective serif details introduced on specific characters, creating a hybrid between a clean sans and a decorative display face. The underlying skeleton is modern grotesque but the selective serifs push it firmly into display territory.
summary: A five-weight display grotesk from Indonesian designer Azzam Ridhamalik, set apart by selective serif details on individual characters that give it a restrained decorative edge.
description: Released in January 2024 by Zarma Type, Galvitra takes a grotesk structure and breaks from convention by introducing subtle serifs on select characters rather than maintaining a clean sans-serif finish throughout. The family spans five weights from Thin to Black, with OpenType features, ligatures and extended Latin support. It suits logo work, headlines and print display applications where a touch of typographic idiosyncrasy is an asset.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type, based in Sukoharjo, Central Java, Indonesia, describes Galvitra as a bold reimagining of the grotesk style for modern display work. The foundry highlights its distinctive character shapes and selective serif details as giving the face depth and visual authority, positioning it for logos, branding and print where projects need something contemporary and eye-catching.

name: Kangmas
classification_notes: Rounded retro display serif in the Cooper Black tradition. Heavy, low-contrast strokes with softened serif terminals and a distinctly chunky silhouette. Two-style family (Regular and true Italic) pitched at branding, logotypes and short headline work.
summary: Kangmas is a chunky retro display serif from Indonesian indie foundry Zarma Type, leaning on Cooper Black's rounded warmth for branding and headline use.
description: Released in 2022 by Zarma Type, Kangmas is a two-style display serif taking Cooper Black as its point of departure, pairing heavy rounded strokes with softened serif terminals. It sits squarely in vintage territory while remaining legible at display sizes. Regular and Italic styles suit branding, logotypes, short headlines and playful editorial contexts that call for visual weight and nostalgic character.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Kangmas as a nostalgic retro serif offered in Regular and true Italic styles. The design draws from Cooper Black and the broader revival of retro aesthetics, combining vintage letterforms with contemporary refinements to balance old-school warmth with present-day clarity.

name: Laqula
classification_notes: Single-weight rough display script with hand-drawn texture and deliberate organic imperfection. Petite x-height with generous ascenders and descenders. Retro/vintage character with brush-lettering feel. 394 glyphs covering Latin Extended-A, with OpenType ligatures and PUA-encoded alternates. Type: foundry.
summary: A single-weight rough script from Indonesian foundry Zarma Type, with hand-drawn texture and a retro outdoor character suited to poster work, logos and travel-themed branding.
description: Laqula is a rough display script built around a petite x-height, generous ascenders and descenders, and the deliberate imperfection of hand lettering. One Regular weight covers 394 glyphs across Latin Extended-A, with OpenType ligatures and PUA-encoded alternates included. Best deployed on posters, postcards and logotypes where a vintage adventure or countryside feel is the brief.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Laqula as a captivating script blending classic charm with modern touches, designed with medium stroke weight and a hand-drawn retro quality – as though each letterform were drawn by hand. They recommend it for travel, outdoor and country-aesthetic work: posters, postcards, logos and old-school styled branding.

name: Lautren
classification_notes: A bold display script built on reversed contrast – thick horizontals, thin verticals – inverting conventional script logic. Single weight, basic Latin only (70 glyphs), with contextual alternates, stylistic sets, ligatures and swash endings via OpenType.
summary: A single-weight reversed-contrast bold script from Zarma Type, designed for display and branding work with a playful summer character and a rich set of OpenType alternates.
description: Lautren inverts conventional script contrast, applying thick horizontals and thin verticals to give familiar letterforms an unexpected, eye-catching quality. Released in 2022 by Azzam Ridhamalik, it includes contextual alternates, stylistic sets, ligatures and swash endings, giving designers considerable range within a single weight. At 70 glyphs it covers basic Latin only, making it best suited to short headline or logotype work rather than extended text.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Lautren as a bold reversed-contrast script drawn from summer vibes, refined to feel neater and smoother than typical display scripts. It was built with contextual alternates, stylistic sets, ligatures and swash endings as standard, and the foundry recommends Adobe software or CorelDraw to take full advantage of the OpenType features.

name: Malrin
classification_notes: Single-weight fatface display typeface with ultra-high contrast and chunky, rounded letterforms. Technically a high-contrast serif in the 19th-century fatface tradition, but classified as display given its purely decorative, large-scale application. Filtered through retro-funk and psychedelic aesthetics rather than classical restraint. Ships with 180+ OpenType alternates and ligatures, PUA-encoded for broad software access.
summary: A single-weight fatface display face from Indonesian indie foundry Zarma Type, built on ultra-bold, high-contrast letterforms with a groovy, psychedelic retro character and over 180 OpenType alternates.
description: Malrin is a chunky, high-contrast fatface designed for headlines, logotypes and posters. It draws on the exuberant tradition of 19th-century fatface type, filtered through a retro-funk sensibility that leans into groovy, psychedelic letterform character. A single weight with an extensive alternate set makes it best suited to expressive display contexts where glyph variety matters more than weight range.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type is an independent display-focused type foundry based in Sukoharjo, Central Java, Indonesia, founded by designer Azzam Ridhamalik. The studio describes Malrin as a chunky retro face drawn from the fatface tradition, conceived around a groovy, funky and psychedelic sensibility. It ships with more than 180 alternate characters and ligatures, PUA-encoded for easy access, and is positioned for logos, posters, headlines, packaging, apparel and advertising.

name: Maltique
classification_notes: Single-weight extra bold display sans with oversized proportions and heavy strokes. Sharp outer corners contrast with smooth, melted inner curves – a detail that gives the letterforms warmth despite their bulk. No italic, condensed or mono variants. PUA-encoded alternates included.
summary: A single-weight extra bold display sans with oversized proportions and melted inner curves that sits somewhere between retro charm and clean contemporary weight.
description: Maltique is a chunky display sans designed by Azzam Ridhamalik of Zarma Type, released in 2026. Its defining detail is the contrast between sharp outer corners and smooth, rounded inner curves – a combination that softens the impact of very heavy strokes without losing authority. It covers 88+ Latin-based languages and suits branding, packaging and editorial headlines where a confident, personality-led voice is needed.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Maltique as a bold display typeface with oversized proportions, heavy strokes and sharp outer corners offset by melted inner curves. The design blends retro confidence with modern simplicity, aiming to feel playful without tipping into childishness, with broad Extended Latin coverage across more than 88 languages.

name: Manteman
classification_notes: Single-weight monoline script with a vintage lettering influence and clean, contemporary execution. Relies on 208 OpenType glyph alternates and swash variants rather than discrete weight or width variants. No upright, condensed or mono sibling styles.
summary: A single-weight monoline script with vintage roots and 208 glyph alternates, positioned for logotypes, apparel and branding that needs a handcrafted feel.
description: Manteman is a monoline script from Zarma Type, drawing on vintage lettering traditions while keeping the overall construction clean and contemporary. It ships with 208 glyph alternates and swash variants, giving designers room to vary texture within a single weight. Extended Latin coverage with support for accents and diacriticals makes it deployable across branding, signage and apparel projects.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Manteman as a blend of vintage and modern typography, built around 208 glyph alternatives including swash versions and full OpenType features. The foundry recommends it for logotype, branding, digital lettering, apparel, signage and advertising work; it ships in OTF, TTF, WOFF and WOFF2 formats with tiered commercial licensing.

name: Marige
classification_notes: High-contrast display serif with bold, structured letterforms bridging classical proportions and contemporary weight. Single-weight family. Extensive OpenType features: stylistic sets, standard and discretionary ligatures, oldstyle figures, small caps, and PUA-encoded characters. 550+ glyphs.
summary: Marige is a bold, high-contrast display serif from Zarma Type suited to headlines, posters and fashion branding where a structured, confident letterform does the work.
description: Designed by Azzam Ridhamalik at Zarma Type, Marige combines classical serif proportions with a contemporary heaviness built for large-scale use. It ships with 550+ glyphs and a solid set of OpenType features – stylistic sets, ligatures, oldstyle figures and small caps – giving designers more reach than a typical single-weight display font. It performs well in logo design, editorial headers and fashion contexts across Latin-script languages.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type is an independent type foundry based in Sukoharjo, Indonesia, run by hand lettering artist and type designer Azzam Ridhamalik. The studio specialises in distinctive display typefaces aimed at branding, editorial and packaging work.

name: Megren
classification_notes: Experimental hybrid display face combining copperplate script uppercase with a clean sans-serif lowercase in a single font file. The contrast between the two registers creates a retro-modern character suited to high-impact display contexts. No weight variations; relies on the inherent contrast within the design.
summary: A single-weight display face pairing copperplate script uppercase with clean sans-serif lowercase, built for branding and fashion applications.
description: Megren merges copperplate script capitals with a clean sans-serif lowercase into one font file, producing a hybrid display face that plays a retro elegance against stripped-back geometry. Released by Zarma Type in 2022, it suits logo design, editorial headings and fashion or cosmetics branding where a single typographic move needs to carry a lot of character. OpenType features and PUA-encoded characters extend the glyph set beyond the standard Latin range.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Megren as an experimental display typeface combining a simple clean sans-serif with an elegant copperplate script, at once modern and fashionable while carrying a nostalgic retro character.

name: Mogan
classification_notes: Single-weight rounded bubble display typeface. Thick, organic letterforms with exaggerated curves and a consistently bubbly rhythm throughout. No weight variants, no italics, no condensed or mono cuts. PUA-encoded alternates included.
summary: Mogan is a single-weight retro bubble display face from Zarma Type, built for bold, cheerful headline and packaging work.
description: Its rounded, thick letterforms draw on a vintage aesthetic to produce a consistently bubbly rhythm. Suited to food branding, café menus, social media graphics and product packaging where an upbeat retro personality is the point. There are no weight or style variants – one display cut, one register.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Mogan as a font made to turn simple words into bold, cheerful statements. Organic curves and soft, thick shapes carry a nostalgic feel with contemporary appeal. Recommended for posters, food branding, product packaging, café menus, social media graphics and retro wordmarks.

name: Monigue
classification_notes: Single-weight bold condensed geometric sans-serif; strong vertical rhythm with Y2K-era modernist references; designed strictly for display use. The entire face is condensed – there is no separate condensed subfamily.
summary: A single-weight bold condensed display sans with Y2K-era geometric rigour, built for high-impact headlines, wordmarks and poster work.
description: Monigue is a bold condensed display sans-serif by Azzam Ridhamalik, released through Zarma Type in 2024. Tall, geometric letterforms with strong vertical rhythm give it a commanding presence at display sizes, drawing from the clean modernism of early 2000s design. It covers 370+ glyphs across Extended Latin with OpenType features, ligatures and PUA-encoded characters, and is available free for commercial use.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type, an independent foundry based in Sukoharjo, Central Java, Indonesia, describes Monigue as a bold, strong condensed font designed to make a statement. It channels the sleek modernist aesthetic of early 2000s design with a contemporary edge, and is offered free for commercial use with multiple licensing tiers available for extended applications.

name: Mufteya
classification_notes: A display serif drawing on retro conventions while keeping proportions clean enough for contemporary use. Two styles only – upright and oblique (labelled Slant). Stylistic alternates, ligatures and PUA encoding give compositional variety without additional weights. No true italic or condensed cut.
summary: A two-style retro display serif from an Indonesian indie foundry, built for vintage logos, poster headers and magazine titles.
description: Mufteya pairs a Regular and an oblique Slant cut with extended Latin support, stylistic alternates, ligatures and PUA encoding to give designers compositional variety within a compact family. The design sits between a modern serif and a retro display face, with proportions balanced enough for editorial work at headline size. It suits vintage logo work, poster design and decorative text overlays more than body copy.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describe Mufteya as a modern serif with a retro touch that allows users to combine stylistic alternates and unique character shapes to get variations quickly. They position it as a ready solution for vintage logos, layout design, poster headers, magazine titles and stylised text overlays.

name: Myntro
classification_notes: Contemporary geometric display sans with condensed proportions drawn from mid-century Mediterranean poster design. Sold as a five-weight family with a variable font file covering the full weight range. Features ligatures and stylistic alternates.
summary: A bold geometric display sans with condensed proportions and five weights, referencing mid-century Mediterranean poster design.
description: Myntro takes mid-century Mediterranean poster culture as its visual reference, building condensed geometric letterforms on a sturdy structural backbone. Five named weights run from Light to Bold, with a single variable font file covering the full range. It is pitched at editorial headlines, brand identities, packaging and event graphics.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type positions Myntro as a contemporary bold display sans serif shaped by the visual confidence of mid-century Mediterranean poster culture. The family spans five weights with variable font support, extended Latin character coverage, and includes ligatures, stylistic alternates and PUA-encoded characters.

name: Native Letter
classification_notes: All-caps bold sans serif system with an oblique variant, shipped alongside a companion connecting script in both upper and lower case. No true italic – oblique only. No condensed or mono variants. PUA-encoded characters and stylistic alternates included.
summary: Native Letter pairs an all-caps block sans in Regular and Oblique with a flowing script companion, designed for punchy headlines in travel and hospitality branding.
description: A display font system by Azzam Ridhamalik at Zarma Type, released in November 2025. The sans component offers two all-caps styles – Regular and Oblique – while the script delivers both uppercase and lowercase letterforms for visual contrast. Built for travel posters, event flyers and lifestyle campaigns where personality outranks precision.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type bills Native Letter as a modern bold font built to deliver punchy headlines and sun-soaked personality in one confident voice – blocky sans shapes paired with a flowing script companion for travel, hospitality and lifestyle branding where clarity matters but character leads the way.

name: Nebulica
classification_notes: Geometric grotesk with deliberate monospace influences; distinctive inktraps and slanted stems contribute to its structured, tech-inflected character; nine-weight family with variable font support; no italic or condensed variants.
summary: A nine-weight geometric grotesk from Zarma Type blending grotesk structure with monospace discipline through inktraps and slanted stems, producing a sharp, tech-inflected voice.
description: Nebulica is a geometric sans-serif released by Zarma Type in 2024, drawing on both grotesk convention and monospace precision to produce a clean, modern character. Inktraps and slanted stems add visual tension without sacrificing legibility, and variable font support gives fine-grained control across the weight range. It suits UI design, editorial layouts and branding with a futuristic or minimalist direction, though the absence of italics limits its usefulness in extended text.
foundry_blurb: Nebulica is positioned as an experimental typeface that merges the clean lines of grotesque typography with the structured discipline of monospaced design. Inktraps and slanted stems deliver visual consistency across weights, while the extended character set covers 88+ languages with more than 435 glyphs, including arrows, symbols, ligatures and PUA-encoded characters. The family targets futuristic layouts, minimal branding, editorial work and interface design.

name: Nekta
classification_notes: Single-weight geometric display sans-serif with heavy strokes, rounded terminals and tight letterfit. Oblique variant only – no true italic. Chunky proportions and curved cuts place it firmly in the sporty/display bracket; not suited to running text.
summary: A chunky geometric display sans from an Indonesian indie foundry, built for sporty headlines and bold graphic work at large sizes.
description: Nekta is a single-weight geometric display sans released by Zarma Type in 2025. Heavy strokes, rounded terminals and tight letterfit give it a confident, punchy presence at display sizes, making it a reasonable pick for event posters, sports branding and packaging. The family is limited to Regular and Oblique – there are no additional weights or a true italic – so its range of application is narrow.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type positions Nekta as a modern sans-serif with confident weight, rounded corners and playful geometry designed to turn short words into powerful headlines. The heavy letterforms, curved cuts and tight rhythm give each word strong visual presence, while the rounded details keep the tone approachable rather than aggressive. Generous counters and clean spacing extend its usefulness from menu boards and event posters to product labels, sports tickets and large-format signage.

name: Nobulina
classification_notes: Hybrid display typeface pairing condensed sans-serif letterforms with inktrap detailing and script-like alternates. Available in two styles – Regular and Inktrap – with 60+ discretionary ligatures, stylistic alternates, and PUA-encoded characters. Condensed proportions are intrinsic to the design; there are no separate width variants. Intentionally experimental, referencing brutalist and industrial aesthetics.
summary: Nobulina presses condensed sans letterforms against inktrap-laced strokes and script-like alternates, designed for brutalist posters, editorial headlines and high-contrast branding work.
description: Designed by Azzam Ridhamalik at Zarma Type in Indonesia and released in October 2025, Nobulina sits in deliberate tension between structural rigidity and expressive movement. Two styles – Regular and Inktrap – each bring a different register to that contrast, supported by over 60 discretionary ligatures and stylistic alternates. It suits album covers, campaign visuals, typographic posters and any context where formal opposition is the point.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Nobulina as a collision of contrast and control: condensed sans letterforms set tightly against inktrap-laced strokes and script-like alternates. The design combines brutalist edge with fluid expressive movement, intended for experimental branding, brutalist posters, editorial headlines, album artwork, tech event visuals and urban signage.

name: Rayton Brink
classification_notes: Geometric rounded sans-serif with consistently soft, rounded terminals and even stroke weights throughout. Single weight only. Designed for display and branding use rather than continuous text. Sits in the broad category of friendly consumer-facing rounded sans-serifs alongside faces like Nunito or Poppins, though with a more overtly playful character.
summary: A single-weight geometric rounded sans from Indonesian foundry Zarma Type, aimed at playful branding, packaging and display work.
description: Rayton Brink is a geometric rounded sans-serif with soft terminals and even stroke weights, built for warmth and legibility at display sizes. It targets brand identity, packaging and headline use rather than running text, occupying the familiar territory of friendly consumer-facing type. The family ships in Regular and Italic with multilingual support across ten languages including English, Indonesian, Dutch and Welsh.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type positions Rayton Brink as a brand-personality typeface that brings joy, clarity and approachability to identities through smooth thick curves and a playful presence. The foundry recommends it for lifestyle, food, tech and children's markets, from homepage headlines and product packaging to app UI and bold posters.

name: Rollions
classification_notes: Single-weight all-caps display serif with rounded slab-style serifs. Intended for logotypes and short headers. Includes OpenType features: discretionary ligatures, stylistic sets and PUA-encoded characters. Extended Latin coverage for multilingual use.
summary: A single-weight all-caps display serif with rounded slab serifs, suited to logotypes and short headers.
description: Rollions is an all-caps display serif released by Zarma Type in 2024, built around rounded slab-style serifs that give it a soft, characterful presence at large sizes. The family is a single style with OpenType support including discretionary ligatures, stylistic sets and PUA-encoded characters. Extended Latin coverage makes it usable across a range of Latin-script languages.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Rollions as a unique all-caps display serif with rounded serifs, designed to serve as a memorable logotype or header alongside cleaner, contrasting typefaces. It ships with stylistic sets, discretionary ligatures and multilingual Latin character support, available in OTF, TTF, WOFF and WOFF2 formats.

name: Stretchy Organic
classification_notes: Rough compressed display face with deliberate ink-bleed texture and blurred edges referencing letterpress and street poster printing. Single weight, no italics. The compression is inherent to the design rather than a variant.
summary: A single-weight compressed display face with rough, hand-stamped texture, built for posters, streetwear graphics and zine layouts that want type with genuine attitude.
description: Stretchy Organic draws from letterpress tradition and street poster culture, with deliberately blurred ink edges and tightly compressed proportions. It ships in a single bold weight, which suits its purpose – this is type for display moments and branding graphics, not body copy. The organic imperfection is consistent enough to feel intentional, making it a credible choice for streetwear, music event and indie publishing projects.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type positions Stretchy Organic as carrying the spirit of hand-stamped letterpress, sun-bleached street posters and ink-soaked zine culture. Every letterform has slightly blurred edges that mimic real print pressure, compressed proportions that demand vertical space, and a raw, tactile quality. The foundry targets streetwear and apparel branding, food and beverage packaging, music event posters, editorial headlines and any project requiring bold organic type with texture and attitude.

name: Thourenz
classification_notes: All-caps monoline display typeface with a uniform stroke weight throughout. Six stylistic variants span clean through heavily distressed finishes – Inked, Rough, Stamp, Outline and Outline Rough alongside the base Regular. No italic or condensed cuts. The consistent monoweight construction and retro letterforms place it firmly in the display-only camp.
summary: An all-caps monoline display typeface with six stylistic variants ranging from clean to heavily distressed, suited to retro-facing logos, posters and merchandise.
description: Thourenz is an all-caps monoline display typeface built on a consistent stroke weight throughout. Six variants – Regular, Inked, Rough, Stamp, Outline and Outline Rough – let designers control how worn the letterforms appear, from sharp to heavily degraded. Over 500 glyphs with OpenType features cover logos, packaging, posters and print-on-demand merchandise.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describe Thourenz as a monoline vintage typeface that brings vintage aesthetics together with modern typographic construction, shipping in six styles with over 500 glyphs, OpenType features and underline options for mixing and matching characters in playful retro layouts.

name: Trimen Drawing
classification_notes: Bold handdrawn display face with thick, expressive strokes and deliberate organic imperfections. The two variants (Regular and Round) are stylistic alternates rather than a conventional weight axis. Strictly a headline and logotype face – not suitable for text setting.
summary: A fat handdrawn display face with thick strokes and deliberate organic imperfections, available in Regular and Round variants.
description: Trimen Drawing is a bold handdrawn display typeface built around thick strokes and playful curves, with organic imperfections that give it an authentic handlettered quality. The family ships in two styles – Regular and Round – and includes over 100 discretionary ligatures along with PUA-encoded alternates for expressive typesetting. It suits food packaging, streetwear branding, editorial headlines and youth campaigns where bold personality takes priority over typographic precision.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type is an independent foundry based in Sukoharjo, Central Java, Indonesia, making display typefaces for designers who want work that stands out. Founded by Azzam Ridhamalik, the studio focuses on expressive, character-driven display fonts and offers custom type design alongside standard licensing.

name: Trinstam
classification_notes: High-contrast classical serif with display proportions and a retro-vintage inflection. Single weight, no italic or condensed. Generous OpenType alternate glyph set (120+) gives stylistic range within one style. Proportions read as transitional-influenced but the decorative character pushes it firmly into display territory.
summary: A single-weight high-contrast display serif with a retro-classical character, designed for logos, editorial headers and packaging that needs period flavour.
description: Trinstam is a high-contrast display serif with classical proportions and a retro edge, built for headline use in editorial, branding and packaging work. It ships as a single weight with over 120 alternate glyphs and ligatures accessible via OpenType, giving designers stylistic variation within one style. Character coverage runs to 114 glyphs including basic Western European accented characters, making it best suited to straightforward Latin-script projects.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type is an independent display type foundry based in Sukoharjo, Central Java, Indonesia, founded by designer Azzam Ridhamalik. The foundry produces display typefaces for designers who want distinctive, memorable work, and offers commercial licensing across desktop, web, app and broadcast media alongside custom font design services.

name: Trivenia
classification_notes: Two-style display typeface inspired by the Baldur Type Specimen. Classic letterforms with modernised, softened curves giving a vintage-psychedelic character. The Inked style adds an organic, hand-printed texture over the base forms. Intended for large-scale use in branding and logotype applications.
summary: Trivenia is a two-style retro display typeface with classically rooted letterforms and softened curves, available in a clean Regular and a textured Inked variant suited to branding and logotype work.
description: Trivenia draws on classic display lettering with a modernised approach to its curves, landing in a zone that reads as vintage without being slavishly period-accurate. Two styles are offered: the clean Regular and an Inked version that overlays an organic, hand-printed texture across the forms. It is best used at large sizes for branding, poster design and logotype work where its quirky, psychedelic edge can register properly.
foundry_blurb: Trivenia carries a classic shape with a modern touch on its curves. It ships in two styles, Regular and Inked, to give designers more room to be creative with their projects.

name: Verilet
classification_notes: All-caps only display typeface with a semi-vintage, elegant character. Three-weight family (Regular, Bold, Outline) designed strictly for headline and identity work; no lowercase, no italic. PUA-encoded alternates and ligatures extend the glyph set beyond the standard Latin range.
summary: An all-caps vintage display sans in three cuts – Regular, Bold and Outline – designed for logos, headlines and luxury branding.
description: Verilet is an all-caps display typeface from Zarma Type with a semi-vintage elegance suited to fashion, wedding and luxury contexts. The family ships in three weights – Regular, Bold and Outline – with over 400 glyphs including ligatures, stylistic alternates and PUA-encoded characters. It covers extended Latin and is intended for use at headline scale in branding, editorial and packaging.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type is an independent type studio run by Azzam Ridhamalik in Sukoharjo, Central Java, Indonesia. The foundry produces display and decorative typefaces aimed at branding, packaging and editorial markets, distributed via its own site and Creative Market.

name: Vonder
classification_notes: Bold display typeface with a Victorian-influenced sans-serif skeleton, offered in three texture variants rather than traditional weight grades: Regular (clean), Rough (distressed), and Stamped (inked relief). Single effective weight throughout. No italic or condensed cuts.
summary: A bold vintage display family in three texture cuts – Regular, Rough and Stamped – built for retro branding, poster work and apparel.
description: Vonder is a bold display typeface from Azzam Ridhamalik at Zarma Type, drawing on Victorian-era letterforms and offered in three variants that each add a layer of surface wear. Regular is solid and clean; Rough introduces a distressed, gritty quality; Stamped replicates the look of an inked relief print. The family is designed for large-scale display use in vintage branding, signage, poster design and apparel graphics where a hand-crafted, lived-in character is the point.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describe Vonder as a vintage, rough-textured bold display font with the potential to elevate any creation needing a retro aesthetic. The full family ships in Regular, Rough and Stamped cuts, covering uppercase, lowercase, numerals, punctuation, ligatures, OpenType features, PUA-encoded characters and Extended Latin multilanguage support, in OTF, TTF, WOFF and WOFF2 formats.

name: Zatiyan
classification_notes: Bold single-weight display sans-serif with classical letterform influences and ink traps. Retro and pop-art inflected character; tagged by the foundry as bold, vintage, urban and chic. Limited to one regular style with 101 glyphs covering extended Latin.
summary: A bold, single-style display sans-serif from Central Java blending modern structure with classical letterform details and ink traps for retro-edged graphic work.
description: Zatiyan is a display typeface designed by Azzam Ridhamalik of Zarma Type in Central Java, Indonesia, first released in 2022. A single regular weight combines bold modern sans-serif construction with classical letterform references and ink traps, giving it a retro and pop-art inflection. It suits logo work, poster headlines and layouts where character outweighs typographic versatility.
foundry_blurb: Zarma Type describes Zatiyan as a bold modern typeface with a thread of classic letter styles, built for graphic design across logos and layouts. Ink traps add legibility alongside a distinctive edge intended to make the work stand out.
